_readme: This file is the signature -> repo map for scripts/triage.py, the act-loop that
replaced per-message LLM triage in #alerts. A 'signature' is `source:external_id`
from ~/.hermes/watchdog.db's `events` table (source = one of slack_alert, uk,
docker_homelab, docker_vps, hermes_log).
MATCH TARGETS (this is the part that was missing in the first draft of this file):
`rules`/`ignore` are matched against TWO candidate strings per event, in order, first
match wins across BOTH: `source:external_id` (the raw form) and
`source:normalize_title(title)` (the human-readable form, same normalize_title() as
scripts/watchdog-poll.py). For a grouped source (slack_alert, hermes_log) these are
usually the SAME string, since that source's external_id already IS
normalize_title(title) — see aggregate_slack_batch()/poll_hermes_logs(). For a state
source (uk, docker_homelab, docker_vps) they differ: uk's external_id is an opaque,
unglobbable UptimeKuma monitor id ('204'), so `uk:macmini-dev-host-push` (the
title-derived target) is what makes that source mappable at all — a rule written
against the numeric id would break the moment the monitor is recreated.
Matching is glob-style (Python fnmatch: `*`, `?`, `[seq]`). `rules` matched
top-to-bottom, first match wins. `ignore` is checked FIRST, before `rules` AND
before `ignoreUnstructuredSlackProse` below — a match sends the item straight to
state `ignored`: never carded, never escalated. No match in either list -> the item
stays unmapped (state `new`, never escalates, carried silently) and its signature
shows up in a once-a-day 'unmapped triage signatures' digest so this file can grow
deliberately instead of silently missing real problems.
`ignoreUnstructuredSlackProse` (bool) is a STRUCTURAL filter, not a glob list: any
`slack_alert` item whose title does not start with a recognized bot-alert shape
(`[`, the siren emoji, checkmark, warning, or a bold-mrkdwn warning) is ignored.
WHY IT EXISTS: before #alerts was silenced (see config.yaml), Hermes replied in
that channel to every message, and watchdog-poll.py's slack_alert poller ingested
those replies right alongside real bot alerts — hundreds of German/English
sentences ('Alles grün. :ok_hand:', '1Password ist aktuell rate-limited...') sitting
in `events` as if they were alert signatures, dozens still open. Silencing the
channel stops NEW ones; this flag is what keeps the existing backlog from getting
carded on this file's first run. A single boolean beats thirty hand-written prose
globs and doesn't need updating every time Hermes phrases a reply differently.
Every `repo` value MUST resolve under `root` in config/dispatch-repos.json and MUST
NOT appear in that file's `deny` list — scripts/triage.py checks the deny list
itself before ever shelling out, so a rule naming a denied repo just silently never
escalates (logged to stderr) rather than crashing, but it is still a bug in this
file, not a feature. `homelab-private` is denied and 'shelfmark' below is why it is
in `ignore` rather than mapped to it: shelfmark is a third-party image
(ghcr.io/calibrain/shelfmark) running in the private compose file — nothing to
dispatch an investigation against even if the repo were reachable.
The HyperDX-origin alerts (job.reaped, podcast.failed, vps-edge-*, ...) map to
`vps`, not to the service they're ABOUT (research-gateway, audio-gateway, ...) —
their threshold/definition lives in vps/observability/alerts/*.json, which is
where the fix (a threshold, a query) actually lands.
To extend: run
sqlite3 ~/.hermes/watchdog.db "SELECT source, external_id, title FROM events
WHERE resolved_at IS NULL ORDER BY first_seen DESC LIMIT 40;"
and add a rule (or an ignore pattern) for anything real that shows up unmapped —
remembering a `uk` rule almost always wants the title-derived target, e.g.
`uk:some-monitor-name-push`, never the bare numeric id.
